subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Use of Social Media
overview: Social media and other digital tools can be used for good or for harm. In this sub-strand you will name digital devices used at home and at school, learn appropriate ways to use social media, and practise integrity by doing what is right even when nobody is watching the screen.

lessons.title: Digital devices and appropriate use
objectives: List digital devices used at home and at school.
Describe appropriate ways of using social media.
lessons.intro: A phone, a tablet, a computer or a television can play a gospel song or a lesson. The same device can also carry a stranger's chat or a bad video. Appropriate use means choosing the good use and refusing the harmful one.
lessons.notes:
### Digital devices
A digital device is a machine that stores or shares information using electronic signals. In groups, list devices you know or use. Not every home has all of them.

- Mobile phone or smartphone
- Tablet
- Computer or laptop
- Television
- Radio
- A camera, or the camera in a phone

At school you may use a computer, a tablet or a radio in a lesson. At home you may watch a television or use a parent's phone. Name only the devices you truly know. Do not pretend the school has a device it does not have.

### What social media is
Social media means ways of sending messages, photos and videos to other people through the internet, for example chats and video sites. Many Grade 4 learners meet it on an adult's phone.

### Appropriate ways to use it
Appropriate means fitting and right.

- Ask a parent, guardian or teacher before you use a device.
- Use it for learning, for a gospel song, or for a video clip based on the Bible.
- Keep the time short. Stop when the adult says stop.
- Be kind in any message you send. Do not insult or spread lies.
- Do not chat with strangers. A person online may not be who the photo shows, and some strangers want to harm children.
- Do not share your full name, the name of your school, your home area, your phone number or your photos with people you do not know.
- Do not open links sent by strangers.
- Do not look at or forward bad pictures.
- If a message frightens you or asks you to keep a secret, tell a parent or teacher at once.

Using a device to listen to a gospel song or to watch a Bible story is a good use. Chatting with a stranger is not. The device is not evil. The way we use it is the moral choice.

keyWords.meaning: an electronic machine such as a phone, tablet, computer, radio or television
internet ways of sharing messages, photos and videos with other people
fitting and right for the user and for the situation
a person you do not know, including a person who messages you online

examples.problem: A message from someone you have never met says, "Send a photo of yourself and the name of your school." What is the appropriate response?
steps: Sharing a photo and a school name with a stranger is not safe.
Appropriate use means refusing and telling an adult.
examples.answer: Do not send the photo or the school name. Tell a parent, guardian or teacher.

activity.title: Devices we know and how to use them well
materials: A digital device if the teacher provides one
A gospel song or a Bible video clip
steps: In groups, list some digital devices that you know or use at home and at school.
In pairs, discuss appropriate use of social media.
Say why you should not chat with strangers online.
With the teacher, use a digital device to listen to a gospel song or watch a video clip based on the Bible.

practice.question: Name four digital devices a learner might know at home or at school.
practice.answer: Any four: mobile phone, tablet, computer, laptop, television, radio or camera.

practice.question: What is social media?
practice.answer: Ways of sharing messages, photos and videos with other people through the internet.

practice.question: Give three appropriate ways of using social media or a digital device.
practice.answer: Any three: ask permission, use it for learning or a gospel song or Bible video, keep the time short, be kind, and do not chat with strangers or share private details.

practice.question: Why should you not chat with strangers online?
practice.answer: They may not be who they claim to be, and some strangers want to harm children.

summary: Digital devices include phones, tablets, computers, radios and televisions.
Use them with permission, for learning and for what is good.
Do not chat with strangers or give them your photos and private details.

lessons.title: Integrity when nobody is watching
objectives: Explain how integrity applies to social media.
Choose to do right even when no adult is watching the screen.
lessons.intro: It is easy to do right when a parent is looking over your shoulder. Integrity is doing the same right thing when the adult has walked into the kitchen and the screen is still on.
lessons.notes:
### Integrity
Integrity means being honest and doing what is right even when it costs you, and even when no one sees. On social media, integrity looks like this:

- You do not open a bad video just because nobody is in the room.
- You do not send a cruel message and then pretend you did not.
- You do not use a parent's phone in secret after you were told to stop.
- You do not help a friend cheat by sending test answers.
- You tell the truth if you accidentally open something wrong.

God sees what people do not see. Integrity is living as if that is true, because it is true. The value is not fear of being caught only. It is a desire to do the right thing always.

### When no one is watching
Picture three moments:

1. The gospel song has ended. A new video, not chosen by your parent, starts to play and it is ungodly. Integrity switches it off.
2. A classmate messages, "Don't tell the teacher I took the pen." Integrity refuses to hide the wrong.
3. A stranger sends a friendly chat. Integrity does not reply and does not keep it a secret.

In each moment the device has not changed. The person using it has a choice. Appropriate use and integrity belong together. Appropriate use is the rule. Integrity is keeping the rule when it would be easy to break it.

### A simple promise
Before you touch a device, ask: Did an adult allow this? Is this kind? Would I be happy for my parent and for God to see it? If the answer is no, stop. Then tell a trusted adult about anything that already went wrong. Owning up is part of integrity too.

Using social media responsibly is a way of loving God and loving other people. It also keeps children safer. A learner who will not chat with strangers protects himself or herself and sets an example for friends.

keyWords.meaning: doing what is right and honest even when nobody is watching
using something in the way you were trusted to use it
facts such as your school, home, phone number and photos that strangers should not have

examples.problem: Your parent leaves the room during a Bible video. The next clip is an ungodly movie, and no one will know if you watch it. What does integrity do?
steps: Integrity means doing right even when no one is watching.
An ungodly movie is not an appropriate use of the device.
The right action does not depend on being caught.
examples.answer: Switch it off or go back to what you were allowed to watch, and tell your parent if you need help.

activity.title: Right use even when unseen
materials: A digital device if the teacher provides one
steps: In pairs, discuss appropriate use of social media, including what to do when an adult is not watching.
Say why you should not chat with strangers online.
Act the three moments: a bad video starts, a friend asks you to hide a wrong, a stranger sends a chat. Show the choice that has integrity.
If a device is available, listen again to a gospel song or a Bible clip, then stop when the teacher says stop.

practice.question: What is integrity?
practice.answer: Doing what is right and honest even when nobody is watching.

practice.question: Give two ways to show integrity when using social media.
practice.answer: Any two: do not open bad videos in secret, do not send cruel messages, do not use a phone against an adult's instruction, do not hide a classmate's wrong, and do not reply to strangers.

practice.question: A stranger's chat arrives while you are alone. What should you do, and why?
practice.answer: Do not reply and do not keep it secret. Tell a parent or teacher. Strangers online may want to harm children, and integrity refuses hidden chats.

practice.question: Why should you do the right thing even when no one is watching the screen?
practice.answer: Because integrity means the right thing does not depend on being seen. God sees, and the choice still matters.

summary: Integrity is honesty and right action even when the screen is unwatched.
Switch off what is ungodly, refuse secret chats, and do not hide other people's wrongs.
Ask whether an adult allowed the use, whether it is kind, and whether God would be pleased.

quiz.question: Which of these is a digital device?
quiz.explanation: A tablet is an electronic device. The others are personal or school items.

quiz.question: Name two digital devices used at home or at school.
quiz.answer: Any two: phone, tablet, computer, laptop, television, radio or camera.
quiz.explanation: Learners list devices they know or use.

quiz.question: Social media is:
options: Ways of sharing messages, photos and videos on the internet
quiz.explanation: Social media shares messages and pictures through the internet.

quiz.question: Which use of a device is appropriate?
options: Watching a Bible video with permission
quiz.explanation: A Bible video with an adult's permission is a right use.

quiz.question: Why should you not chat with strangers online?
options: Because every stranger is a teacher
Because they may not be who they seem, and some want to harm children
Because the Bible forbids all songs
quiz.explanation: Strangers online are unsafe to chat with.

quiz.question: Which details should you not give to someone you do not know online?
quiz.answer: Your full name, school, home area, phone number and photos.
quiz.explanation: Private details help a stranger to find or harm a child.

quiz.question: Integrity when using social media means:
options: Doing right only when a parent is watching
Doing right even when nobody is watching
quiz.explanation: Integrity is right action without needing an audience.

quiz.question: An ungodly video starts while you are alone. What should you do?
options: Switch it off and tell a parent if you need help
Call a stranger to discuss it
quiz.explanation: Integrity refuses the bad video even in private.

quiz.question: You want to do the right thing even when no one is watching. What value is that?
quiz.explanation: The desire to do right unseen is integrity.

quiz.question: Before you use a device, which question helps you choose well?
quiz.answer: Any one: Did an adult allow this? Is it kind? Would I want my parent and God to see it?
quiz.explanation: These questions join appropriate use with integrity.
